fingerprint.structure: 3 slides: attitude selfie with meme caption (hook) → 'before' mirror selfie in the thing people judge (baggy clothes) → 'after' mirror selfie, identical pose/room/framing, in the reveal outfit (payoff)
fingerprint.hook: Clapback meme: 'When someone says "[judging question about you]" like [sarcastic version of what they assume]'; paired with a smug, unbothered selfie expression; promises a reveal on the next slides
fingerprint.camera_motion: Phone photos: slide 1 casual close-up selfie (lying down, wink, lollipop = attitude); slides 2–3 full-body mirror selfies, phone covering face, same spot and pose so only the outfit changes
fingerprint.pacing: 3 slides; text only on slide 1 (about 20 words, 4 lines); slides 2–3 have no text so the contrast lands on its own
fingerprint.text_overlay: TikTok native font (TikTok Sans / Classic), white, sentence case, thin dark shadow, centered horizontally, middle of the frame, 4 short lines; quotation marks around the judging question
fingerprint.audio: Trending confident song (Bow Bow Bow – Zeddy Will), not original
fingerprint.arc: Mild annoyance → attitude → reveal/flex; payoff = the before/after contrast; emotions: humor, validation, confidence

units.text: When someone says "why do you always wear baggy clothes" like my body was gonna disappoint
units.visual: close-up selfie lying on an outdoor couch, wink, lollipop, grey sweatshirt; siding wall background
units.layout: face lower half, text centered mid-frame

units.visual: full-body mirror selfie, oversized white sweatshirt + baggy dark pants, bright living room, dog in foreground
units.layout: subject centered, head in top third

units.visual: same mirror, pose and room; fitted plum long-sleeve mini dress + heels; shows the physique

product: None named; the reveal outfit/body is the 'product'. For brands: the reveal item (dress, activewear, fitted piece)
proof_device: None (the before/after photo pair is the proof)
series: Single post; a repeatable meme template
caption: Emoji only (🤫🤫🤫) + 5 hashtags; the caption adds nothing, the slides carry it
language: English, first person, sassy and confident, meme phrasing ('when someone says… like…')
